subject: plotting ancestral ranges for thousands of species

messages.author: b6c73fdfb6befaf8
messages.subject: plotting ancestral ranges for thousands of species
parts:
Dear colleagues,

I was wondering if anyone has a solution to plot a nice and legible ancestral ranges tree using 5,000 sp.
I've already played with the height and width arguments of the pdf() command, with other arguments (cex means, tipcex, statecex, splitcex, titlecex, plotsplits), and tried to edit in Adobe Illustrator. However, given the high number of species, the editing takes so long and not good. And I have not seen ancestral ranges plot using thousands of species in the literature.

Does anyone know if BiogeoBEARS export the data to make the tree in another program/script (e.g. figtree, ggtree, phytools)? If yes, how do I do that?

Cheers,
Fernanda

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] plotting ancestral ranges for thousands of species
parts:
Hi,
Thanks for the question.   This is a very challenging problem, because biogeographic problems often have hundreds of different possible ranges, and if each gets a different color, it rapidly becomes unreadable.  The BioGeoBEARS defaults use a "color-mixing" strategy (the range AB has a color that mixes the individual colors of A and B), which helps a bit, but probably doesn't help much for 5000 species.

Your best bet is to construct your own custom graphic in R.  The key item you need is the results object. If it is named "res":

names(res) -- has the saved outputs

res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node -- this has the ancestral range probabilities at each node under the model.  The rows are nodes in the tree (use the function prt(tr) to see a table with the rows in the same order).  The columns are the states, in order, e.g. null, A, B, C, AB, AC, BC, ABC

res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_bottom_below_node -- this has the same, for the branch bottoms below each branch top

So, I would suggest something like:

* choose the most probable state at each branch top & branch bottom
* give all "complex" ranges some generic color like grey (maybe only color in the top 10 ranges or something)
* color the branches rather than the nodes
* perhaps use a "radial" tree or some other format used for huge trees

You'd have to figure out how to paint branches on such trees, I haven't done this myself, but you could consult whatever R packages there are for plotting huge trees.

Cheers!
Nick
